title: Minecraft Voxel Sandbox
text:
Build an original browser-based voxel survival sandbox inspired by Minecraft, substantial enough to feel like a real world rather than a tech demo.

Include deterministic procedural terrain with biomes, caves, resources, structures, weather and day/night; persistent worlds; mining/building; inventory and crafting; survival, creatures and combat; farming/smelting/storage; and a simple automation or circuit system. Movement, streaming, UI, audio and feedback should feel polished, with impressive landscapes, caves, water and lighting.

Done when the core explore → gather → craft → build → survive → progress loop is fully playable, persistent, visually convincing, and worth returning to.

title: GTA Open World Action
text:
Build an original browser-based open-world crime/action game inspired by GTA-style freedom and chaos.

Create a dense city with distinct districts, traffic, pedestrians, landmarks, day/night and weather. Support on-foot exploration, third-person combat, weapons, multiple drivable vehicles, escalating police pursuit and escape, plus several authored missions or side activities. Give the world its own characters, tone, locations, vehicles and visual identity.

Done when free-roaming is fun on its own and the driving, combat, wanted system, missions, NPC activity and presentation form one coherent polished game.

title: FNAF Animatronic Horror
text:
Build an original browser-based animatronic survival-horror game inspired by Five Nights at Freddy's surveillance tension.

Create a memorable location, original threats with learnable rules, security cameras, limited defenses/resources, strong audio-visual cues, escalating nights or stages, variable AI, clear win/fail states, secrets or lore, and earned jumpscares. Atmosphere should come from lighting, sound, camera presentation, silhouettes and environmental storytelling.

Done when the player can understand, learn and master the threat system across repeatable tense runs, rather than merely endure random scripted scares.

title: Fortnite Battle Royale
text:
Build an original browser-based third-person battle royale inspired by Fortnite's fast movement, shooting, building and match flow.

Create a colorful island with memorable areas and traversal. Include an airborne drop, responsive gunplay, loot, health/shields, healing, inventory, harvesting, fast structure placement/editing, destructible builds, a shrinking storm, eliminations, and convincing bots or opponents that can move, loot, fight and build.

Done when a complete match works from landing through late-game pressure to victory/defeat and quick replay, with polished feedback, effects, UI and an original art direction.

title: SubwaySurfers Endless Runner
text:
Build an original polished browser-based 3D endless runner inspired by Subway Surfers.

Use responsive lane switching, jumping and sliding/rolling across a continuously varied course with hazards, ramps, tunnels, elevation changes, alternate routes and memorable scenery. Add collectibles, useful powerups, multipliers, challenges, unlocks/upgrades, rising difficulty and convincing chase pressure.

Done when the camera, collision, animation, audio, effects and restart loop make score-chasing fast, readable and addictive.

title: Portal Physics Puzzle
text:
Build an original browser-based first-person physics puzzle game inspired by Portal.

The two-portal system must provide convincing portal views, reliable traversal, natural orientation and momentum preservation, and support physics objects. Create a sequence of original chambers that teach and combine portals with objects, switches, hazards or moving devices, culminating in multi-step momentum-based solutions. Give the facility its own identity and story flavor.

Done when the game has a clear progression, beginning and ending, and feels like a complete polished puzzle game rather than a portal-rendering demo.

title: SpeedGame High Speed Platformer
text:
Build an original browser-based 3D high-speed action platformer inspired by modern Sonic-style games, with an original character and world.

Make movement the star: responsive acceleration, turning, jumping, air control, momentum and satisfying speed mechanics, with reliable high-speed camera behavior. Create substantial levels or a connected campaign with branching routes, verticality, set pieces, enemies, secrets, collectibles and alternate lines, plus times/ranks for replayability.

Done when moving through the world feels exhilarating and mastering faster, cleaner routes is genuinely rewarding.

title: Original Game Blank Canvas
text:
Create an entirely original browser-based game from scratch. Choose the genre, core mechanic, world, characters, progression, structure, art direction and audio direction yourself.

Center it on one distinctive idea with a clear core loop, meaningful decisions, satisfying controls, evolving challenge or progression, authored content, strong game feel and a memorable audiovisual identity.

Done when it feels like a focused finished game with either a real ending or a compelling replayable structure. Surprise me and cook.

title: FL Studio Browser DAW
text:
Build a serious polished browser-based DAW inspired by modern music software such as FL Studio, with an original interface.

Support creating projects, instruments, step sequencing, piano-roll note editing, multi-track arrangement, mixing, audible effects, automation, save/reopen, and real audio render/export. Include several distinct sound sources, at least one editable synth, transport/meters, snapping, zoom/scroll, clip/note editing, mute/solo, volume/pan, and important undo/redo. Include an editable multi-pattern demo song using effects, mixing and automation.

Done when I can make, edit, mix, save, reopen and export an actual short song without the app feeling like a mockup.

title: Astra Showcase Website
text:
Build a polished showcase website for the projects created during Astra testing: gallery, portfolio, experiment archive and launcher.

Give it an original futuristic Astra identity. Use a data-driven project registry with strong cards, visuals, descriptions, status, categories, useful metadata, search/filtering, featured projects, detail views, and launch/repository actions when available. Adding a project entry should update relevant views automatically, and local/offline/in-development/live states must be represented truthfully.

Done when the showcase is polished enough to deserve a card in its own gallery.

title: Daily Ship Log
text:
Build a polished local-first development journal for my AI-agent work with a daily calendar, prompt archive, project/activity history, verified ship log and read-only view of current sessions.

Preserve user prompts chronologically and clearly separate REQUESTED, REPORTED/APPEARS, and independently VERIFIED activity, with confidence for inferred status. Each day should show projects, meaningful events, accomplishments and blockers; ACTIVE NOW should summarize current task, progress, blocker, last activity and confidence. Keep durable cross-day history, fast search, periodic reconciliation/checkpoints, privacy and secret awareness. Provide simple Windows START, STOP, STATUS and OPEN controls without duplicate instances.

Done when I can open any old date and immediately understand what we actually cooked that day.

title: Anime Gacha Action RPG
text:
Build an original polished browser-based 3D anime gacha action RPG with a cohesive original IP.

Create a memorable world, factions, story tone and at least one substantial explorable region. Include roughly 3–4 strong playable characters with consistent designs, personalities, roles, abilities and animations; responsive character-specific combat with dodging and team/switch value; enemies, rewards, traversal, NPC/story moments; progression, quests, party management and save/load. Add a fictional earnable-currency summon system with exciting presentation and collection/upgrades.

Done when it feels like the beginning of a real anime action RPG, with quality and cohesion prioritized over roster size.

title: Roblox Studio Lite
text:
Build a polished browser-based 3D creation tool inspired by Roblox Studio, with an original editor identity.

Include a 3D viewport, hierarchy/explorer, properties inspector, object insertion, transform tools, selection feedback, camera navigation, common primitives/scene objects, editable visual/physics properties, local save/load, and Edit versus Play/Test modes. Play/Test should enter the authored scene with a controllable character or camera and return to Edit without losing work. Include an attractive example scene.

Done when I can build a small scene, play it instantly, return to editing, save it, reopen it and continue naturally.

title: Premiere Pro Lite
text:
Build a polished browser-based nonlinear video editor inspired by professional tools such as Premiere Pro, with an original interface.

Include a media bin, preview monitor, multi-track timeline, playhead/time ruler, transport and inspector/effects area. Support importing browser-compatible video/image/audio, arranging tracks, trimming, splitting, reordering, deleting, scrubbing, seeking, zooming, snapping and previewing the real composition. Add titles/text, transform/opacity, audio volume, useful visual effects/adjustments, at least one transition, local project save/load, and real export/render if practical.

Done when I can make, polish, preview, save, reopen and continue editing a short multi-clip video.

title: Original Rhythm Game + Chart Editor
text:
Build an original polished browser rhythm game with an integrated chart editor that uses the exact same chart format as gameplay.

Use 4–6 lanes with real timing windows, tap notes plus at least one additional note type, combo, score, accuracy, misses, results/grades, pause/restart and offset calibration. Include at least one complete original or generated song with an intentionally authored synchronized chart. The editor must support seeking, note placement/move/delete, hold editing, useful BPM/offset metadata, zoom/scroll, save/load and immediate playtesting.

Done when authoring a chart and jumping straight into a satisfying, readable playtest feels seamless.

title: 3D Animation Editor
text:
Build a compact polished browser-based 3D character animation editor inspired by Moon Animator and Blender's animation workspace.

Include a 3D viewport, ready-to-animate rigged humanoid, rig hierarchy, transform controls, timeline, visible keyframes, playhead, playback and useful easing/interpolation. Support selecting meaningful joints, posing, creating/updating/moving/deleting keyframes, smooth scrubbing, duration changes, multi-joint animation and local save/load. Include a short editable example animation.

Done when I can pose, keyframe, scrub, play smooth motion, save, reload and keep editing like a real little animator.

title: After Effects Lite
text:
Build a polished browser-based motion-graphics/compositing editor inspired by After Effects, focused on a practical core.

Include a composition viewer, layer/timeline panel, playhead, properties/effects inspector and preview controls. Support text, shape, image and background layers; reordering/common layer operations; keyframeable position, scale, rotation and opacity with multiple keyframes, visible markers and useful easing; plus several real visual/compositing effects. Include local save/load and an attractive editable demo composition.

Done when I can build, animate, effect, preview, save and reopen a small multi-layer motion graphic.

title: FNF Style Rhythm Game Original Song
text:
Build a polished original browser-based call-and-response rhythm battle inspired by Friday Night Funkin', with completely original characters, stage, chart and music.

Create at least one full original song with distinct sections, a memorable groove, build/climax and recognizable player/opponent vocal-like phrases. Author the chart around the music so handoffs and intensity feel musical and fair. Include menu → battle → results/retry, four-direction inputs, health tug-of-war, score, combo, misses, accuracy/judgments, pause/restart and expressive beat-reactive performers/stage.

Done when the battle feels like a small finished rhythm-game release worth replaying for the song and performance.

title: 3D Obby Speedrun Game
text:
Build an original polished browser-based 3D obby/speedrun game centered on movement mastery and better times.

Use a compact movement kit whose mechanics work well together, such as run, jump, air control, dash, slide, wall-run or wall-jump. Create one excellent course or a few connected stages with checkpoints, verticality, moving/timed obstacles, shortcuts, alternate routes and advanced lines. Include timer, splits/progress, local personal best, instant restart and medal/rank targets.

Done when the movement feels reliable and satisfying enough that replaying for a cleaner, faster route is the main attraction.

title: Original First Person Horror Game
text:
Build a short polished original browser-based first-person horror game that can be completed in one sitting.

Create a coherent location with environmental storytelling, clear beginning, escalation, climax and real ending. Include responsive interaction, roughly 3–4 interconnected puzzles/objectives, and at least one understandable threat sequence such as stalking, chase or timed escape. Use lighting, spatial audio, ambience, environmental change, silence and pacing for tension rather than relying only on darkness and jumpscares.

Done when it feels authored, memorable and complete rather than like a random dark hallway demo.

title: Physics Sandbox
text:
Build a polished browser-based 3D physics sandbox designed for immediate emergent fun.

Create a compact playground with varied props, articulated/ragdoll objects, explosive or impulse toys and satisfying manipulation tools for grabbing, throwing, freezing, duplicating, deleting, changing useful physical properties, applying forces, creating simple constraints, resetting the world, and experimenting with gravity or slow motion. Objects should collide, stack, topple, roll, connect and scatter convincingly with strong impact feedback.

Done when opening the sandbox immediately makes me want to invent increasingly ridiculous physics experiments.

title: Factory Tycoon Game
text:
Build an original browser-based 3D factory/tycoon game where I physically move around a plot, place machines, build production chains, automate them and expand.

Support the loop start small → place machines → visibly produce/move/process items → sell → reinvest → optimize → expand. Include extractors, conveyors, processors, storage, sellers and later advanced machines, with several meaningful recipes/tiers so routing, bottlenecks, speed, space and throughput matter. Persist the factory locally and make products, machines, status and income satisfying to watch.

Done when I can save, reload and keep optimizing a visibly busy production line I designed.

title: Music Visualizer
text:
Build a polished browser-based music visualizer driven by a user-loaded local audio file.

Include at least three clearly different visual modes, polished transitions, fullscreen, playback/seek/volume, visible timeline, several presets/themes, and a small useful set of intensity/smoothing/sensitivity/effects controls. The visuals should respond meaningfully to rhythm, energy and changing musical sections.

Done when it is expressive and synchronized enough to enjoy watching for an entire song, not merely a spectrum debug view.

title: Game Launcher
text:
Build a polished browser-based game launcher/library inspired by modern PC launchers, with original branding and fictional or local game data.

Include an attractive library and detail experience with cover art, screenshots, descriptions, playtime, achievements, favorites, search/filtering, recently played, install/play/update states and a compact downloads/activity area with believable simulated progress. At least one or two launch flows should open a lightweight browser mini-game or interactive demo.

Done when navigation and interactions feel premium enough that the launcher feels alive rather than like a static dashboard.

title: Character Customizer
text:
Build a browser-based character customizer that produces visibly distinct characters and is fun to experiment with.

Use layered 2D art or a lightweight 3D character. Include meaningful choices such as hair, outfit, colors, face/expression, accessories and body/pose with immediate feedback, plus randomize, reset, several presets, local save/load and a clean photo/preview mode.

Done when repeatedly randomizing and refining characters produces enough variety and polish to stay entertaining.

title: Retro Arcade Hub
text:
Build a browser-based retro arcade hub with 3–4 original mini-games that have genuinely different mechanics and real score-chasing loops.

Use a unified arcade lobby, local high scores, recent runs, immediate controls, strong audiovisual feedback and distinct identities for each game. Every mini-game needs a clear loop, failure state, quick restart and enough depth to stand on its own, plus light arcade-wide progression or unlocks tied to scores.

Done when each cabinet is worth replaying and the collection feels like a real arcade rather than a launcher full of shallow demos.

title: Shader Playground
text:
Build a polished browser-based interactive shader/effects playground that feels like a compact creative tool.

Provide a large live preview with several impressive effects/presets such as distortion, RGB split, glow, noise, pixelation, waves, chromatic effects, scanlines or procedural gradients. Let the user tweak parameters live, load an image or use demo media, save/load presets locally and randomize settings. Include at least one beautiful animated procedural effect requiring no uploaded media.

Done when experimentation is immediate, visual and satisfying.

title: 3D Parkour Playground
text:
Build a polished browser-based 3D parkour/speedrun playground with movement fun enough to practice for its own sake.

Use a responsive kit such as sprint, jump, slide, dash, wall-run or wall-jump. Create one compact timed course built around chaining abilities, with checkpoints, instant restart, personal best, medal targets, intentional shortcuts/advanced routes, and a small practice/free-roam area. Keep camera/FOV, effects, audio and environments exciting but readable.

Done when repeated time-chasing and movement mastery are more compelling than simply exploring the map.

title: Boss Fight Game
text:
Build a polished browser-based game focused almost entirely on one excellent original boss fight.

Give the player responsive movement and a simple satisfying combat kit. Create one memorable boss with readable attacks, strong animation, multiple patterns and at least two distinct escalating phases. Include health, damage feedback, fair readability/invulnerability behavior, strong arena, music/audio, dramatic effects, quick restart, win/lose states, short intro and satisfying victory sequence.

Done when the fight rewards learning patterns and improving execution rather than surviving random unavoidable damage.

title: Rhythm Boss Battle
text:
Build a browser-based rhythm boss battle where music timing directly drives combat.

Create one full original or generated song with multiple sections and rising intensity, then author synchronized rhythm inputs with real timing windows and clear feedback. Successful inputs should meaningfully attack, defend, dodge, charge, counter or otherwise affect the fight, while the boss's phases, attacks and visuals follow the song structure. Include health, score, combo, win/lose states, beat-reactive presentation and instant restart.

Done when the music, chart and combat feel designed together as one encounter rather than layered on top of each other.

title: Physics Destruction Playground
text:
Build a browser-based physics destruction playground centered on emergent fun and satisfying collapse.

Fill a sandbox with physics props and several breakable structures, including at least one designed to collapse spectacularly. Let the user spawn/manipulate objects and destroy things with varied tools such as impulses/explosions, gravity tricks, projectiles or a wrecking ball, with slow motion and quick reset. Use debris, dust, particles, impact audio and strong physical feedback while remaining responsive.

Done when the scene immediately invites increasingly ridiculous destruction experiments.

title: Drone Simulator
text:
Build a polished browser-based 3D drone simulator with convincing but approachable controls.

Let the player fly a small agile drone from FPV and external views through a compact environment with gates, obstacles, elevation changes, tight spaces and memorable landmarks. Include a timed checkpoint/race mode, personal best, quick crash reset and useful telemetry-style HUD.

Done when precision flying, free exploration, line hunting and repeated race attempts all feel satisfying.

title: Fake Malware Desktop Game
text:
Build a safe browser-based fictional desktop horror/puzzle game that convincingly imitates a computer desktop entirely inside the webpage.

Start with believable fake windows, files, apps, folders, messages and terminal-like interfaces, then escalate through impossible files, glitches, strange behavior and visual corruption. Build puzzles around inspecting the fictional system, connecting clues and discovering hidden information, leading to a strong scripted sequence and clear ending. Keep every effect fictional and contained in the page.

Done when it feels creepy, convincing and interactive rather than like a sequence of popups.

title: Racing Time Trial
text:
Build a polished browser-based racing time-trial game centered on handling and chasing faster laps.

Create one excellent track with responsive acceleration, braking and steering plus a satisfying drift, boost or momentum system. Include lap/checkpoint validation, timer, instant restart, personal best, medal/rank targets and a short practice/free-drive option; add a local ghost replay if it fits naturally. Prioritize driving feel, track flow, camera, speed feedback, audio and skid/particle effects.

Done when the "one more run" loop is the strongest part of the game.

title: Conveyor Tycoon
text:
Build a polished browser-based conveyor/factory tycoon where the player physically lays out and optimizes production.

Start with limited money and a compact empty build area. Support placing/rotating/removing extractors, conveyors, processors, storage, sellers and upgrades. Items must visibly travel through the line and machines must transform them into more valuable outputs, with at least three meaningful production tiers/recipes so routing, bottlenecks, throughput and expansion matter. Persist progress locally.

Done when watching and improving the moving factory is satisfying enough to feel like a spatial automation game, not an idle dashboard.

title: Security Camera Horror
text:
Build an original browser-based security-camera survival-horror game.

Place the player in a fixed control room connected to several distinct camera locations. Create original threats with learnable tense rules, limited resources/defenses, and audio-visual clues that require correct responses. Include escalating difficulty, AI variation, clear clock/progression, memorable failure states, quick restart and a satisfying win state.

Done when tension comes from understanding and managing a system under pressure rather than random scares.

title: Interactive Music Video
text:
Build a polished browser-based interactive music video around an original or generated song with multiple sections.

Create an authored audiovisual sequence synchronized to the music, with visuals that react to rhythm/energy and evolve meaningfully across the song. Let the viewer influence the experience through simple mouse, click, keyboard or visual-choice interactions without making passive watching impossible. Include fullscreen and replay, plus seeking if it fits naturally.

Done when it feels like a small music experience worth watching more than once, not merely a visualizer.

title: Multiplayer Parkour Race
text:
Build a polished browser-based multiplayer 3D parkour race for roughly 2–8 players.

Create one excellent compact obstacle course and a responsive movement kit with skill expression, shortcuts, advanced routes and checkpoints that prevent trivial skipping. Players should race simultaneously, see each other clearly, and get live placement, checkpoint progress, finish times and personal bests. Include lobby/ready, synchronized countdown, race state, results, rematch and sensible join/leave handling.

Done when repeated races and time-chasing remain fun and the shared race state stays coherent for everyone.

title: FNF Multiplayer Battle
text:
Build a polished browser-based head-to-head multiplayer rhythm battle for 2 players inspired by FNF's structure and energy, with completely original music, characters and presentation.

Create one full original song with multiple sections and a synchronized directional-note chart with timing windows, combo, misses, accuracy, score and a clear versus/pressure meter. Both players compete on the same song in real time. Include lobby/ready, countdown, battle, results, rematch and opponent-left state, plus expressive performers, beat-reactive backgrounds and strong hit/judgment feedback.

Done when it feels like one coherent shared rhythm battle rather than two score counters side by side.

title: Multiplayer Horror Escape
text:
Build a polished browser-based co-op multiplayer horror escape game for 2–4 players.

Create one atmospheric authored location with a clear beginning, progression arc and escape condition. Players should cooperate on several interconnected objectives/puzzles while facing one original AI threat with readable tense behavior and at least one memorable chase/high-pressure sequence. Include a meaningful teamwork mechanic such as reviving, item handoff, split roles, synchronized interactions or rescue. Keep puzzle/item/door/threat/player state coherent for everyone, with lobby/ready, success/failure and sensible disconnect recovery.

Done when cooperation genuinely matters and the full escape works as a shared experience.

title: Multiplayer Party Minigame Collection
text:
Build a polished browser-based multiplayer party-game collection for roughly 4–8 players.

Create a lobby/ready flow and a match containing at least four short, genuinely different minigames with clear rules, fast pacing, scoring and win/fail conditions. Award points after each round, maintain an overall leaderboard, finish with a podium/winner screen, support easy rematch and handle ordinary joins/leaves gracefully. Use strong audiovisual feedback, playful transitions and readable UI.

Done when the collection feels like replayable party chaos rather than a large shallow content library.

title: Coop Spaceship Crew Game
text:
Build a polished browser-based co-op spaceship crew game for 2–4 players.

Players share one ship and must cooperate through a short mission using interconnected systems such as piloting/navigation, power, shields, repairs, weapons, engines, sensors or life support. Trigger escalating emergencies that force reprioritization and teamwork. Keep ship state, hazards, repairs, mission progress and player interactions coherent for everyone, with lobby/crew-ready, understandable station roles, success/failure and sensible behavior if crew size changes.

Done when the core fantasy is "everyone yelling while fixing the ship," with readable systemic teamwork prioritized over world size.

title: Team Objective Shooter
text:
Build a polished browser-based multiplayer team objective shooter for roughly 4v4 or 5v5 players.

Create one excellent compact arena supporting Team Deathmatch, Capture the Flag and King-of-the-Hill/Control. Include team assignment, respawning, timers, score limits, scoreboard, match-end/rematch flow and a small roster of distinct weapons with clear roles. Movement, aiming, shooting, hit feedback, reloading, damage and deaths should feel responsive. Keep player, objective, score, respawn and match state coherent for everyone, with strong team identity, readable objectives, lobby/ready and sensible disconnect handling.

Done when combat and objective play feel solid enough that one polished arena is more valuable than additional content.
